summary: Strava's main friction themes include: AI overreach, subscription fatigue, UI/UX issues, data privacy concerns, and feature bloat.

themes.name: Data Privacy and Security Concerns
themes.description: Users are concerned about data exposure, such as location leaks from Strava activities, and the app's handling of sensitive information.
themes.recommendation: Enhance data security and transparency around location tracking and data sharing.

themes.name: Feature Bloat and Complexity
themes.description: The app has become more complex with new features, making it harder to use for basic tracking and reducing the appeal of free features.
themes.recommendation: Simplify the interface and prioritize core functionality.

themes.name: Subscription Fatigue and Paywall Expansion
themes.description: More features are being locked behind paywalls, leading to frustration and a perception that the app is becoming less accessible.
themes.recommendation: Re-evaluate paywall strategy to balance monetization and user retention.

themes.name: UI/UX Issues and App Instability
themes.description: Users report bugs, crashes, and UI changes that break workflows, such as private notes scrolling issues and setting resets.
themes.recommendation: Stabilize core features and improve UI consistency across updates.

themes.name: AI Overreach and Inaccurate Insights
themes.description: AI features are seen as repetitive, unhelpful, and often inaccurate, leading to frustration with premium features that don't deliver value.
themes.recommendation: Refine AI insights to be more actionable and relevant to users.
